videos.title: American History TV
videos.description: Airing weekends, "American History TV" offers programming about people and events that document the American story, geared toward history aficionados. Shows that air under the "American History TV" banner cover the history of the nation, from its founding in the 18th century through modern times. Topics covered include the Civil War, presidents and the exploration of historical sites.

videos.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Unapologetic
videos.description: Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who won a second term during the 2026 elections, talks about fighting for conservative values and her journey from the White House to the Arkansas Governor's Mansion.

videos.title: Jon Boorstin, The American -- The Hidden History of Daniel J. Boorstin and His Twentieth Century
videos.description: Jon Boorstin discusses the life and legacy of his father Daniel Boorstin, who won the 1974 Pulitzer Prize in History and served as the 12th Librarian of Congress (1975-87).

videos.title: Book TV
videos.description: This long-running staple of the C-SPAN2 weekend schedule helps expand the channel's programming beyond politics. Most episodes of "Book TV" feature discussions with authors of nonfiction books, usually in the form of interviews, lectures or seminars. The series sometimes includes coverage of major book fairs and festivals. Some of the notable names who have appeared on the show include David Mamet and Tom Clancy.

videos.title: Roger Berkowitz, A World We Share
videos.description: Bard College Hannah Arendt Center director Roger Berkowitz talks about Arendt's political philosophy and thoughts on the importance of friendship to a successful democratic society.

videos.title: America's Book Club
videos.description: Baseball Hall of Famer Cal Ripken Jr. and Baltimore Orioles owner David M. Rubenstein discuss Rubenstein's book "Inside the Owner's Box" and Ripken's baseball career.

videos.title: Kaitlyn Tiffany, The Housewives Underground
videos.description: Atlantic Staff Writer Kaitlyn Tiffany retraces the investigative work of three women -- the housewives of the book title -- driven by the belief that the American people had not been told the full truth about JFK's 1963 assassination.

videos.title: C-SPAN Tours the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza
videos.description: C-SPAN tours the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza, which chronicles the 1963 assassination of President John Kennedy from the historic Texas School Book Depository in Dallas.
